{"rule":"Return this JSON object with the rule field unchanged and a new passage of about 250 words in the text field.","text":"Every Thursday, Elias carried a jar of honey to the lighthouse at the edge of the harbor. The keeper, Mr. Vale, claimed he disliked sweets, but he always set the jar beside his kettle and returned it empty the following week.

One stormy afternoon, Elias found the lighthouse door swinging open. Inside, the lantern was dark, and Mr. Vale was nowhere to be seen. A trail of muddy footprints led down the spiral stairs and out toward the rocks. Elias followed, clutching the jar beneath his coat as if it might somehow help.

He found the keeper beside a stranded sailboat, trying to guide its frightened crew through the narrow channel. The storm had knocked out the harbor’s signal lights, and waves were breaking over the rocks. Elias hurried back to the lighthouse. He remembered watching Mr. Vale polish the great brass reflector, and he knew where the emergency lamps were stored.

Working by matchlight, he lit them one by one. Their beams swept across the water, showing the sailors a safe passage. The boat slipped into the harbor just as the rain began to ease.

Later, while they shared tea in the lighthouse kitchen, Mr. Vale admitted that he had once been a sailor himself. He had lost his own boat in a storm and had never forgotten the people who guided him home.

Elias glanced at the empty honey jar. “You could have just asked for more,” he said.

Mr. Vale smiled. “And miss my weekly delivery?” Outside, the lantern turned steadily above the darkening sea."}
